claims.text: Introducing coherent nanoprecipitates through targeted alloying or processing can improve ductility in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Introducing coherent nanoprecipitates can improve uniform deformability in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The ductility and uniform-deformability improvements can be achieved without sacrificing high strength.
The intervention can preserve impact-induced energy release.
The proposed intervention is the introduction of a controlled amount of coherent nanoprecipitates.
Coherent nanoprecipitates are the structural mediator of the proposed property changes.
Lattice distortion associated with the intervention enhances dislocation mobility.
Lattice distortion associated with the intervention increases slip-system activation.
The intervention is expected to increase ductility by 15–25% relative to alloys without coherent nanoprecipitates.
The intervention is expected to increase uniform deformability by 15–25% relative to alloys without coherent nanoprecipitates.
The proposed effects should hold at high strain rates.
The proposed effects should hold at high temperatures.
The proposed effects depend on alloy composition and microstructure.
The relevant relationships among microstructure, lattice distortion, and mechanical properties are presently understood only to a limited extent.
High-strain-rate tensile testing combined with microstructural analysis can test the hypothesis.
